transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-10
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Myers (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Mateo Ruiz (Redwood CSM), Aisha Khan (Summit Head of ML), Ben Ortiz (Summit Platform), Clara Liu (Summit Security), Danny Park (Product), Erin Moore (Data Eng)

[00:00] Jordan Myers: hey everyone thanks for joining, really excited to kick this off. quick round of intros?
[00:10] Aisha Khan: hi I'm aisha, lead ml at summit analytics, we run realtime inference for customer insights, latency is pretty key for us.
[00:18] Ben Ortiz: ben, platform eng, i'll own infra integration, vpc stuff, cloud networking.
[00:22] Clara Liu: clara from security, i'll handle compliance and audit questions.
[00:26] Jordan Myers: great thanks. priya and mateo from redwood?
[00:30] Priya Shah: hi all, i'm priya, se focused on performance and scaling, i'll lead the technical deep dive and benchmark.
[00:36] Mateo Ruiz: matt, mateo here, csm, i'll help run onboarding and success milestones.
[00:40] Jordan Myers: ok agenda: overview of Redwood onboarding flow, deployment options (hosted, dedicated, private), security checklist, pilot scope and timeline, and assign next steps.

[00:55] Jordan Myers: quick product primer — redwood offers hosted api for quick integration, dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput, and private vpc/on-prem for regulated data. for most early pilots, teams start on a dedicated pool so they get predictable latency while we run benchmarks.
[01:12] Aisha Khan: curious about latency numbers; we do sub-200ms 99p for our current smaller prompts, with larger context maybe 500-800ms. does dedicated get us there?
[01:22] Priya Shah: good question. dedicated gives you pinned gpu capacity and lower tail latency because of constant pools and KV cache warmup; we'll run workload-specific bench. quick caveat — model size and quantization change numbers. we'll propose configs.
[01:40] Ben Ortiz: on networking — we need VPC peering and restrict egress; can you support VPC peering and customer-managed KMS?
[01:48] Jordan Myers: yes, for private deployments we support customer-managed KMS and VPC options; dedicated supports VPC endpoints and private links. mateo i'll follow up with the exact network diagram.
[01:58] Clara Liu: SOC 2 evidence? and do you provide audit logs for token-level access? also data retention policy?
[02:06] Mateo Ruiz: we can share our SOC 2 report and security pack; redwood console provides request-level audit logs, and you can configure retention. we'll share the security whitepaper and KMS integration guide.
[02:20] Clara Liu: good, also SSO/SAML and RBAC — we need role separation for platform vs product.
[02:26] Priya Shah: SSO/SAML and RBAC supported in the Console; you can enforce org-wide rules and scoped api keys.

[02:35] Danny Park: for success criteria, we want: 1) consistent 99p latency under 250ms on core prompts, 2) cost per 1k requests below our current baseline, 3) integration with our analytics pipeline via streaming responses.
[02:48] Jordan Myers: solid. we'll map metrics to those success criteria and define runbooks.

[03:00] Priya Shah: about bench plan — we'll need a redacted sample dataset and the top 20 prompt templates. ideally parity queries that represent your traffic distribution. we'll run both hosted and dedicated configs to compare latency/cost.
[03:15] Erin Moore: we can provide a pared-down dataset, but need guidance on redaction. also how do you handle PHI/PII?
[03:23] Mateo Ruiz: for PHI/PII, we recommend private deployment or dedicated with strict retention controls and KMS; we'll send data handling guidance.

[03:35] Ben Ortiz: curious about model variants and fallbacks. if capacity spikes, do you auto-failover to cheaper models?
[03:42] Priya Shah: yes, smart routing supports fallback to compatible model variants and different capacity tiers; you can set policy for latency vs cost. we also have automatic KV/prefix caching to lower token cost for repeated contexts.

[04:00] Aisha Khan: licensing and cost — what does a pilot cost look like and how do we scale?
[04:08] Jordan Myers: we'll propose a pilot pricing for a short dedicated pool and show the cost break down in the deck. long-term you can reserve capacity for discounts. i'll attach sample unit economics.

[04:25] Clara Liu: one more on encryption — do you support customer HSM or only cloud KMS?
[04:30] Jordan Myers: we integrate with major cloud KMS, and for Private on-prem we can support HSMs as part of the deployment. we'll capture requirements in the security questionnaire.

[04:42] Priya Shah: technical note — for your use case with mixed short/long contexts, we'll probably recommend a quantized 16k-friendly model variant and smaller batch sizes to keep latency tight. we'll test 8k and 16k sequences.
[04:58] Aisha Khan: sounds good. timeline? we want user-facing pilot in 4–6 weeks.
[05:04] Mateo Ruiz: realistic — week 0-1: share docs and data; week 2: bench and initial integration; week 3-4: pilot on dedicated pool; week 5-6: evaluate and decide on reserved commit.

[05:20] Danny Park: who owns infra work on our side? ben and erin will drive; aisha will own success metrics.
[05:26] Ben Ortiz: confirmed.

[05:30] Jordan Myers: recap of next steps — redwood (jordan/priya/mateo) will send onboarding deck, security pack, SSO guide, and provisioning steps. summit (aisha/ben/er) will share sample prompts and network contact. schedule deep dive — priya will lead bench.
[05:48] Aisha Khan: can you also send a list of required IAM roles and firewall IPs?
[05:53] Mateo Ruiz: yes i'll include that in the onboarding doc.

[06:00] Jordan Myers: perfect, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the deep dive and provisioning window. thanks everyone.

[06:08] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hears around product names, e.g., sometimes "Redwood Dedicated" heard as "red wood dedicated"; speaker overlap at 03:35.

Recap / explicit next steps:
- Jordan to send onboarding deck, pricing, SOC2 and security pack, SSO guide, and network diagram (due 2026-08-12).
- Priya to prepare benchmarking plan and runbench with sample queries (target week of 2026-08-24).
- Summit to provide redacted dataset and prompt list (due 2026-08-17).
- Mateo to provision trial Dedicated pool and invite Summit team to Console (target 2026-08-14).

Shared artifacts referenced: onboarding_deck_v1.pdf (link in CRM), security_questionnaire.xlsx (link), bench_plan_template.csv (link).

End of transcript.
